    38:             + (login__users__combined_var | selectattr("state", "defined") | selectattr("state", "ne", "absent") | map(attribute="primary_group", default="None"))
    39:             + (login__users__combined_var | selectattr("state", "undefined") | map(attribute="primary_group", default="None")))
    40:             | flatten | unique }}'
    41: 
    42:   - ansible.builtin.debug:
    43:       msg:
    44:         - 'Required Groups:'
    45:         - '{{ login__required_groups }}'

    47:   - name: 'Create the required groups'
    48:     ansible.builtin.group:
    49:       name: '{{ item }}'
    50:       state: 'present'
    51:       local: true # this is required for servers which are using FreeIPA, for example
    52:     loop: '{{ login__required_groups }}'
    53: 
    54:   # Needed by the linger tasks below: `loginctl` resolves the account name and fails with
    55:   # `Failed to look up user <name>: No such process` if it does not exist (yet), and stopping the
    56:   # user manager requires the UID.
    57:   - name: 'getent passwd'
    58:     ansible.builtin.getent:
    59:       database: 'passwd'
    60: 
    61:   # Lingering has to be switched off before the account is removed, for two reasons: `loginctl`
    62:   # no longer resolves a deleted account, and lingering keeps a `user@<uid>.service` running
    63:   # without an active session, which makes `userdel` refuse with `user <name> is currently used
    64:   # by process <pid>`.
    65:   - name: 'loginctl disable-linger {{ item["name"] }} # for items with state=absent'

    69:     loop: '{{ login__users__combined_var }}'

    74:       - 'item["state"] | d("present") == "absent" or not (item["linger"] | d(false) | bool)'

    76:   # `loginctl disable-linger` only asks logind to stop the user manager and returns immediately,
    77:   # so `userdel` in the next task would still hit its processes. Stopping the unit blocks until
    78:   # it is really gone. It is a no-op for users without a running manager.
    79:   - name: 'systemctl stop user@{{ ansible_facts["getent_passwd"][item["name"]][1] }}.service # for items with state=absent'

    81:       name: 'user@{{ ansible_facts["getent_passwd"][item["name"]][1] }}.service'
    82:       state: 'stopped'
    83:     loop: '{{ login__users__combined_var }}'
    84:     loop_control:
    85:       label: '{{ item["name"] }}'
    86:     when:

    96:       home: '{{ item["home"] | d(omit) }}'
    97:       name: '{{ item["name"] }}'

    99:       # the ternary does not do lazy evaluation, so both the true and false statement are evaluated.
   100:       # therefore, `d()` is needed so that `password_hash()` does not fail,
   101:       # even though the result is not used in the end
   102:       password: '{{ (item["password"] | d(None)) | ternary(
   103:             (
   104:               item["password"] | d()
   105:               | ansible.builtin.password_hash("sha512", (65534 | random(seed=inventory_hostname) | string))

   111:       system: '{{ item["system"] | d(false) }}'
   112:     loop: '{{ login__users__combined_var }}'
   113:     loop_control:
   114:       label: '{{ item["name"] }}'

   120:     loop: '{{ login__users__combined_var }}'
   121:     loop_control:
   122:       label: '{{ item["name"] }}'
   123:     when:
   124:       - 'item["state"] | d("present") != "absent"'
   125:       - 'item["linger"] | d(false) | bool'

   148:     # the name must match the kickstart file: https://github.com/Linuxfabrik/kickstart/blob/main/lf-rhel.cfg#L231
   149:     community.general.sudoers:
   150:       name: 'linuxfabrik'
   151:       group: '{{ login__passwordless_sudo_group }}'
   152:       commands: 'ALL'
   153:       runas: 'ALL' # allow switching to any other user
   154:       nopassword: true
   155:       state: 'present'
   156:     when: 'login__passwordless_sudo_group is defined and login__passwordless_sudo_group | length > 0'

   159:     - 'login'

   163: 
   164:   # /etc/login.defs is owned by the shadow-utils (RHEL) / login (Debian) package, and its
   165:   # content differs heavily between distributions and even minor releases. We only manage a
   166:   # handful of policy keys, so we edit those lines in place with lineinfile instead of
   167:   # templating the whole distro-owned file (which would mean maintaining one verbatim copy

   169:   # template-over-lineinfile preference in CONTRIBUTING.

   172:   # does not retroactively re-age existing accounts (the role does not run chage on them).
   173:   - name: 'Set password policy and umask in /etc/login.defs'
   174:     ansible.builtin.lineinfile:
   175:       path: '/etc/login.defs'
   176:       regexp: '^{{ item["key"] }}\b'
   177:       line: '{{ item["key"] }} {{ item["value"] }}'
   178:       backup: true
   179:     loop:
   180:       - key: 'PASS_MAX_DAYS'
   181:         value: '{{ login__login_defs_pass_max_days }}'
   182:       - key: 'PASS_MIN_DAYS'
   183:         value: '{{ login__login_defs_pass_min_days }}'
   184:       - key: 'PASS_WARN_AGE'
   185:         value: '{{ login__login_defs_pass_warn_age }}'
   186:       - key: 'UMASK'
   187:         value: '{{ login__login_defs_umask }}'
   188:     loop_control:
   189:       label: '{{ item["key"] }}'
   190: 
   191:   tags:
   192:     - 'login'
   193:     - 'login:login_defs'

     2: # The following variables will be set by the runner of this playbook:

    14: # scm_refspec: a refspec to fetch in addition to obtaining version

    28: - hosts: localhost

    30:   connection: local
    31:   name: Update source tree if necessary

    40:         - delete

    42:     - name: Update project using git

source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Reach a `.local` host over the tailnet when mDNS cannot resolve it - i.e. when
     3: # the playbook runs away from home.
     4: #
     5: # inventory.yml names LAN hosts by their mDNS name (ubuntu-cube.local) because
     6: # that works at home even when Tailscale is down. Away from home the opposite is
     7: # true: mDNS resolves nothing, and the same box is reachable only by its tailnet
     8: # name (ubuntu-cube, MagicDNS), where Tailscale SSH answers on :22. This probes
     9: # mDNS ONCE per host from the controller and, on a miss, points ansible_host at
    10: # the bare name. It costs nothing at home and about 5 s per host away (avahi's
    11: # resolution timeout) - which is why this is a pre-task and not an ansible_host
    12: # template in group_vars: a templated connection var is re-evaluated per task,
    13: # and 5 s x every task is a play that never finishes.
    14: #
    15: # Include in pre_tasks of any play targeting `.local` hosts, and set
    16: # `gather_facts: false` on the play - fact gathering connects BEFORE pre_tasks
    17: # and would fail on the unresolved name. Gather afterwards if the play needs
    18: # facts:
    19: #   - name: ...
    20: #     hosts: ubuntu-cube.local
    21: #     gather_facts: false
    22: #     pre_tasks:
    23: #       - ansible.builtin.include_tasks: lan_or_tailnet.yml
    24: #       - ansible.builtin.setup:
    25: #
    26: # Hosts not ending in .local are left alone.
    27: 
    28: # check_mode: false - the command module is SKIPPED under --check, which would skip the
    29: # probe, skip the fallback, and make a --check run fail on the unresolved name while the
    30: # real run works. The probe is a read-only lookup on the controller; running it in check
    31: # mode changes nothing.
    32: - name: Probe mDNS for {{ inventory_hostname }}
    33:   ansible.builtin.command:
    34:     cmd: getent ahosts {{ inventory_hostname }}
    35:   register: lan_or_tailnet_mdns
    36:   changed_when: false
    37:   failed_when: false
    38:   check_mode: false
    39:   delegate_to: localhost
    40:   when: inventory_hostname is match('.*\.local$')
    41: 
    42: - name: Reach {{ inventory_hostname }} over the tailnet instead
    43:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    44:     ansible_host: "{{ inventory_hostname | regex_replace('\\.local$', '') }}"

1: ---
     2: # Real sshd on an alternate port, UGOS (UGREEN NAS) flavor.
     3: #
     4: # The Ubuntu hosts get their alternate port from sshd_alt_port by extending the stock
     5: # sshd's listen config. That approach is closed on UGOS: the vendor owns sshd_config
     6: # (global ForceCommand wrapper, admin-account passthrough — see rustd_backup_nas's
     7: # README for the field story), and its SFTP subsystem serves a chrooted share view
     8: # (/docker, /home, /storage) instead of the real filesystem. Shell exec passes through
     9: # the wrapper fine, so the rustd.xyz panel's command features (wipes, snapshots) work —
    10: # but every SFTP read against a real path fails ("Operation unsupported"), which is what
    11: # broke the panel's moderator roster, snapshot listing, blueprint scan and map fetch on
    12: # NAS-hosted servers (rustd.xyz#456).
    13: #
    14: # So instead of extending the vendor sshd, this runs a SECOND stock sshd instance with
    15: # its own clean config on the same port number sshd_alt_port uses everywhere else:
    16: #
    17: #   :22   -> vendor sshd, untouched (UGOS UI, wrapper, and whatever the vendor patches)
    18: #   :2222 -> stock OpenSSH: key-only auth, one allowed user, normal internal-sftp
    19: #
    20: # Same account, same groups, same filesystem as the wrapper shell — so pointing the
    21: # panel's credential at :2222 changes nothing about exec behaviour and simply makes
    22: # SFTP see the real filesystem. It also future-proofs the NAS against the Tailscale SSH
    23: # badge ever being enabled here (the exact port-22 interception sshd_alt_port exists for).
    24: #
    25: # The vendor config is never read or written; a firmware update that stomps
    26: # /etc/systemd/system or /etc/ssh/sshd_config_alt is repaired by re-running this role.
    27: 
    28: - name: Install the alternate sshd config
    29:   become: true
    30:   ansible.builtin.copy:
    31:     dest: /etc/ssh/sshd_config_alt
    32:     content: |
    33:       # Managed by ansible (sshd_alt_port_ugos). See the role for why this exists.
    34:       Port {{ sshd_alt_port_ugos_number }}
    35:       PidFile /run/sshd-alt.pid
    36:       PermitRootLogin no
    37:       PasswordAuthentication no
    38:       KbdInteractiveAuthentication no
    39:       UsePAM yes
    40:       AllowUsers {{ sshd_alt_port_ugos_allow_users }}
    41:       X11Forwarding no
    42:       Subsystem sftp internal-sftp
    43:     owner: root
    44:     group: root
    45:     mode: "0644"
    46:     validate: /usr/sbin/sshd -t -f %s
    47:   notify: Restart ssh-alt
    48: 
    49: - name: Install the ssh-alt systemd unit
    50:   become: true
    51:   ansible.builtin.copy:
    52:     dest: /etc/systemd/system/ssh-alt.service
    53:     content: |
    54:       # Managed by ansible (sshd_alt_port_ugos). See the role for why this exists.
    55:       [Unit]
    56:       Description=OpenSSH on the alternate port (clean config, no UGOS wrapper)
    57:       After=network.target
    58: 
    59:       [Service]
    60:       ExecStartPre=/usr/sbin/sshd -t -f /etc/ssh/sshd_config_alt
    61:       ExecStart=/usr/sbin/sshd -D -f /etc/ssh/sshd_config_alt
    62:       ExecReload=/bin/kill -HUP $MAINPID
    63:       KillMode=process
    64:       Restart=on-failure
    65: 
    66:       [Install]
    67:       WantedBy=multi-user.target
    68:     owner: root
    69:     group: root
    70:     mode: "0644"
    71:   notify: Restart ssh-alt
    72: 
    73: - name: Enable and start ssh-alt
    74:   become: true
    75:   ansible.builtin.systemd_service:
    76:     name: ssh-alt
    77:     enabled: true
    78:     state: started
    79:     daemon_reload: true

    12:       - tar
    13:     state: present
    14:     update_cache: true

    17: # Deliberately the tarball rather than the `steamcmd` apt package. That package is i386-only,
    18: # so installing it means `dpkg --add-architecture i386` — a system-wide change that doubles apt
    19: # metadata and invites i386 library sprawl on a host that otherwise has none, all for one test
    20: # rig. (Multiverse is already enabled on ubuntu-cube; the package still has no candidate purely
    21: # because no foreign architecture is registered.) The tarball is self-contained and needs only
    22: # the 32-bit runtime above.
    23: - name: Create the steamcmd directory
    24:   tags: rust-test
    25:   become: true
    26:   ansible.builtin.file:
    27:     path: "{{ rust_test_server_steamcmd_dir }}"
    28:     state: directory
    29:     mode: '0755'
    30:     owner: "{{ rust_test_server_user }}"
    31:     group: "{{ rust_test_server_user }}"

    41:     creates: "{{ rust_test_server_steamcmd_dir }}/steamcmd.sh"

    43: # Owned by the panel's SSH user directly, rather than the group-membership dance the
    44: # containerised servers need (compscidr/iac#486). The panel writes here to snapshot,
    45: # rewrite the seed and delete map files; owning the tree outright is the simplest way
    46: # to grant that, and this host runs nothing else that needs the directory.
    47: - name: Create the server directory
    48:   tags: rust-test
    49:   become: true
    50:   ansible.builtin.file:
    51:     path: "{{ rust_test_server_root }}"
    52:     state: directory
    53:     mode: '0755'
    54:     owner: "{{ rust_test_server_user }}"
    55:     group: "{{ rust_test_server_user }}"
    56: 
    57: # Deliberately NOT guarded with `creates:`. Rust ships updates that break servers —
    58: # on 2026-08-06 one removed BasePlayer.violationLevel and killed a plugin outright —
    59: # so a task that installs once and never updates again is the wrong shape for the
    60: # thing it manages. `app_update` is a no-op when already current, so running it every
    61: # time is cheap; the cost is one steamcmd invocation per play.
    62: - name: Install or update the Rust dedicated server

    64:   become: true
    65:   become_user: "{{ rust_test_server_user }}"
    66:   ansible.builtin.command:
    67:     cmd: >-
    68:       {{ rust_test_server_steamcmd_dir }}/steamcmd.sh
    69:       +force_install_dir {{ rust_test_server_root }}
    70:       +login anonymous
    71:       +app_update 258550 validate
    72:       +quit
    73:   register: rust_test_server_install

    75:   # it actually wrote something, so report changed only in the latter case rather than
    76:   # claiming a change on every single run.
    77:   changed_when: "'already up to date' not in rust_test_server_install.stdout"
    78:   failed_when: rust_test_server_install.rc != 0
    79:

    81: # ~/.steam/sdk64 and, when it is missing, InitGameServer returns false and Rust then
    82: # dereferences the null platform in SteamInventory.LoadItemDefinitions:
    83: #
    84: #   Couldn't initialize Steam Server (InitGameServer(0,30015,30016,3,"2632") returned
    85: #   false - error: Failed to load module '/home/jason/.steam/sdk64/steamclient.so')
    86: #   NullReferenceException at Steamworks.SteamInventory.GetDefinitions ()
    87: #
    88: # The failure is a long way from its cause: map generation runs to completion first, so
    89: # the server looks like it is booting normally for minutes before dying. The container
    90: # image provides this path already, which is why only the bare-metal server needs it.
    91: #
    92: # sdk64 ONLY: RustDedicated is 64-bit and the loader named sdk64. A 32-bit link is what
    93: # 32-bit dedicated servers need and would be cargo cult here.
    94: - name: Create the Steam SDK directory
    95:   tags: rust-test
    96:   become: true
    97:   become_user: "{{ rust_test_server_user }}"
    98:   ansible.builtin.file:
    99:     path: "{{ rust_test_server_home }}/.steam/sdk64"
   100:     state: directory
   101:     mode: '0755'
   102: 
   103: - name: Link steamclient.so where the Steamworks loader looks for it
   104:   tags: rust-test
   105:   become: true
   106:   become_user: "{{ rust_test_server_user }}"
   107:   ansible.builtin.file:
   108:     src: "{{ rust_test_server_steamcmd_dir }}/linux64/steamclient.so"
   109:     dest: "{{ rust_test_server_home }}/.steam/sdk64/steamclient.so"
   110:     state: link
   111:     # steamcmd unpacks the library on first run, not at unarchive time, so on a first
   112:     # play this link is created before its target exists.
   113:     force: true
   114:     follow: false
   115: 
   116: # Rust creates this itself on first boot, but seed.env has to be in it BEFORE that boot
   117: # — start.sh refuses to launch without one — so the role cannot wait for the game.
   118: - name: Create the save directory
   119:   tags: rust-test
   120:   become: true
   121:   ansible.builtin.file:
   122:     path: "{{ rust_test_server_data_dir }}"
   123:     state: directory
   124:     mode: '0755'
   125:     owner: "{{ rust_test_server_user }}"
   126:     group: "{{ rust_test_server_user }}"
   127: 
   128: # Moved, not recreated: this file holds the seed of the map the server is CURRENTLY
   129: # running, and writing a fresh one would silently change the map at the next restart.
   130: #
   131: # Ordered before the create below so that create's `force: false` sees the migrated file
   132: # and leaves it alone. `creates`/`removes` make this a no-op once done, and on a host
   133: # that never had the old layout.
   134: - name: Move a seed.env left at the install root by the pre-2026-08-19 layout
   135:   tags: rust-test
   136:   become: true
   137:   ansible.builtin.command:
   138:     # argv, not a cmd string: a path carrying whitespace — from an override, or a
   139:     # rust_test_server_identity someone gives a space — would otherwise split into extra
   140:     # arguments and mv would move the wrong thing or fail.
   141:     argv:
   142:       - mv
   143:       - "{{ rust_test_server_root }}/seed.env"
   144:       - "{{ rust_test_server_data_dir }}/seed.env"
   145:     creates: "{{ rust_test_server_data_dir }}/seed.env"
   146:     removes: "{{ rust_test_server_root }}/seed.env"
   147: 
   148: # The seed lives in its own file so a wipe can rotate it without rewriting the launch
   149: # script, and it lives in the SAVE directory because that is the path rustd.xyz derives
   150: # the file it rewrites from — the same place compscidr.rust_gameserver keeps it
   151: # (`rust_gameserver_data_dir`). Anywhere else and the panel's wipes cannot change the
   152: # seed at all; see rust_test_server_data_dir for what that looked like.
   153: - name: Create seed.env (never overwritten — wipes rotate it at runtime)
   154:   tags: rust-test
   155:   become: true
   156:   ansible.builtin.copy:
   157:     content: "RUST_SERVER_SEED={{ rust_test_server_seed }}\n"
   158:     dest: "{{ rust_test_server_data_dir }}/seed.env"
   159:     mode: '0644'
   160:     owner: "{{ rust_test_server_user }}"
   161:     group: "{{ rust_test_server_user }}"
   162:     force: false
   163: 
   164: - name: Install the launch script
   165:   tags: rust-test
   166:   become: true
   167:   ansible.builtin.template:
   168:     src: start.sh.j2
   169:     dest: "{{ rust_test_server_root }}/start.sh"
   170:     mode: '0755'
   171:     owner: "{{ rust_test_server_user }}"
   172:     group: "{{ rust_test_server_user }}"
   173: 
   174: - name: Install the systemd unit
   175:   tags: rust-test
   176:   become: true
   177:   ansible.builtin.template:
   178:     src: rust-test.service.j2
   179:     dest: /etc/systemd/system/rust-test.service
   180:     mode: '0644'
   181:     owner: root
   182:     group: root
   183: 
   184: # Both the boot-time enablement and the current state follow rust_test_server_service_enabled,
   185: # which now defaults to true -- so by default this starts the server and enables it at boot.
   186: # Override the variable to false and this stops it and leaves it disabled instead, which is
   187: # how the unsupervised case (#340) is reproduced across a deploy.
   188: - name: Set the service state
   189:   tags: rust-test
   190:   become: true
   191:   ansible.builtin.systemd_service:
   192:     name: rust-test
   193:     enabled: "{{ rust_test_server_service_enabled }}"
   194:     state: "{{ 'started' if rust_test_server_service_enabled else 'stopped' }}"
   195:     daemon_reload: true

name: roles/ssl/tasks/build_certificate_chain.yml
review_question: Is this Ansible artifact excessively large and in need of decomposition?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Certificate Chain Building Tasks
     3: # --------------------------------
     4: # Inputs:
     5: #   - ca_cert_path: PEM file containing one or more trusted CA certificates
     6: #     (root and/or intermediate, in any order).
     7: #   - cert_path: PEM file containing the signed server certificate.
     8: #     May be leaf-only or include any subset of intermediates and/or the root,
     9: #     in any order.
    10: #
    11: # Output:
    12: #   - {{ ssl_file_dir_final }}/{{ service_name }}.chain — properly ordered
    13: #     "leaf -> intermediate(s) -> root" chain. For partial chains where no
    14: #     self-signed root is available, the walk stops at the topmost cert that
    15: #     has a known parent in the trust pool.
    16: #
    17: # Algorithm:
    18: #   1. Split both ca_cert_path and cert_path into individual cert files.
    19: #   2. Identify the leaf in cert_path: the cert whose Subject is not the
    20: #      Issuer of any other cert in cert_path (handles arbitrary input order).
    21: #   3. Use the non-leaf certs from cert_path as -untrusted bridges and run a
    22: #      single `openssl verify -CAfile <bundle> -untrusted <bridges>
    23: #      -partial_chain <leaf>`. This validates the chain cryptographically and
    24: #      handles DoD-style partial chains via -partial_chain.
    25: #   4. Walk Issuer -> Subject across the union of all certs (cert_path +
    26: #      ca_cert_path), starting from the leaf, to emit the ordered chain.
    27: #      OpenSSL has already proven the chain is valid; the walk only sorts
    28: #      the certs into output order.
    29: 
    30: - name: Create temp directory for individual certificates
    31:   tempfile:
    32:     state: directory
    33:     suffix: cert_chain
    34:   register: temp_dir
    35: 
    36: - name: Build and Verify Certificate Chain
    37:   shell: |
    38:     set -euo pipefail
    39: 
    40:     TEMP_DIR='{{ temp_dir.path }}'
    41:     CA_CERT_PATH='{{ ca_cert_path }}'
    42:     CERT_PATH='{{ cert_path }}'
    43:     OUTPUT_CHAIN='{{ ssl_file_dir_final }}/{{ service_name }}.chain'
    44: 
    45:     # 1. Split both input files into individual cert files. The `n>0` gate
    46:     #    drops any leading lines (whitespace, comments, BOM) before the first
    47:     #    BEGIN CERTIFICATE marker so the glob does not pick up junk files.
    48:     awk 'BEGIN{n=0} /BEGIN CERTIFICATE/{n++} n>0 {print > ("'"$TEMP_DIR"'/cert."n".pem")}' "$CERT_PATH"
    49:     awk 'BEGIN{n=0} /BEGIN CERTIFICATE/{n++} n>0 {print > ("'"$TEMP_DIR"'/ca."n".pem")}'   "$CA_CERT_PATH"
    50: 
    51:     cert_files=( "$TEMP_DIR"/cert.*.pem )
    52:     ca_files=(   "$TEMP_DIR"/ca.*.pem )
    53:     if [ ! -e "${cert_files[0]}" ]; then
    54:       echo "ERROR: no certificates found in cert_path ($CERT_PATH)" >&2
    55:       exit 1
    56:     fi
    57:     if [ ! -e "${ca_files[0]}" ]; then
    58:       echo "ERROR: no certificates found in ca_cert_path ($CA_CERT_PATH)" >&2
    59:       exit 1
    60:     fi
    61: 
    62:     subj_of() { openssl x509 -in "$1" -noout -subject -nameopt RFC2253 | sed 's/^subject=//'; }
    63:     iss_of()  { openssl x509 -in "$1" -noout -issuer  -nameopt RFC2253 | sed 's/^issuer=//';  }
    64: 
    65:     # 2. Identify the leaf in cert_path:
    66:     #    the cert whose Subject is NOT the Issuer of any other cert in cert_path.
    67:     LEAF=""
    68:     for f in "${cert_files[@]}"; do
    69:       f_subj=$(subj_of "$f")
    70:       is_parent=false
    71:       for g in "${cert_files[@]}"; do
    72:         [ "$g" = "$f" ] && continue
    73:         if [ "$(iss_of "$g")" = "$f_subj" ]; then
    74:           is_parent=true
    75:           break
    76:         fi
    77:       done
    78:       if ! $is_parent; then
    79:         LEAF="$f"
    80:         break
    81:       fi
    82:     done
    83:     if [ -z "$LEAF" ]; then
    84:       echo "ERROR: could not identify leaf certificate in cert_path ($CERT_PATH)" >&2
    85:       exit 1
    86:     fi
    87: 
    88:     # 3. Collect non-leaf certs from cert_path as bridging intermediates.
    89:     BRIDGES="$TEMP_DIR/bridges.pem"
    90:     : > "$BRIDGES"
    91:     for f in "${cert_files[@]}"; do
    92:       [ "$f" = "$LEAF" ] && continue
    93:       cat "$f" >> "$BRIDGES"
    94:     done
    95: 
    96:     # 4. Verify the chain. -partial_chain permits stopping at a trusted
    97:     #    intermediate (DoD/enterprise PKI without root in the bundle).
    98:     if [ -s "$BRIDGES" ]; then
    99:       openssl verify -CAfile "$CA_CERT_PATH" -untrusted "$BRIDGES" -partial_chain "$LEAF" >&2
   100:     else
   101:       openssl verify -CAfile "$CA_CERT_PATH" -partial_chain "$LEAF" >&2
   102:     fi
   103: 
   104:     # 5. Walk Issuer -> Subject across all available certs to emit the chain
   105:     #    in leaf -> intermediate(s) -> root order. Dedupe by Subject (one cert
   106:     #    per Subject DN) using a file as the seen-set: this is robust to
   107:     #    Subject DNs that happen to contain unusual characters which would
   108:     #    collide with an in-memory delimiter.
   109:     pool=( "${cert_files[@]}" "${ca_files[@]}" )
   110: 
   111:     SEEN="$TEMP_DIR/seen.txt"
   112:     : > "$SEEN"
   113:     : > "$OUTPUT_CHAIN"
   114:     current="$LEAF"
   115:     safety=0
   116:     while [ -n "$current" ]; do
   117:       safety=$((safety + 1))
   118:       if [ "$safety" -gt 32 ]; then
   119:         echo "ERROR: chain walk exceeded 32 hops, aborting (possible cycle)" >&2
   120:         exit 1
   121:       fi
   122: 
   123:       c_subj=$(subj_of "$current")
   124:       c_iss=$(iss_of "$current")
   125: 
   126:       if ! grep -Fxq -- "$c_subj" "$SEEN"; then
   127:         cat "$current" >> "$OUTPUT_CHAIN"
   128:         printf '%s\n' "$c_subj" >> "$SEEN"
   129:       fi
   130: 
   131:       # Self-signed -> a trust anchor, stop walking.
   132:       if [ "$c_subj" = "$c_iss" ]; then
   133:         break
   134:       fi
   135: 
   136:       # Find parent in the pool (Subject == Issuer of current cert).
   137:       parent=""
   138:       for f in "${pool[@]}"; do
   139:         [ "$f" = "$current" ] && continue
   140:         if [ "$(subj_of "$f")" = "$c_iss" ]; then
   141:           parent="$f"
   142:           break
   143:         fi
   144:       done
   145: 
   146:       # No parent found -> partial chain, stop here.
   147:       [ -z "$parent" ] && break
   148:       current="$parent"
   149:     done
   150: 
   151:     echo "Chain written to $OUTPUT_CHAIN" >&2
   152:   args:
   153:     executable: "{{ shell_executable }}"
   154:   register: build_chain_result
   155:   changed_when: build_chain_result.rc == 0

    26: #
    27: # The section below deals with disabling and masking services that need to be
    28: # disabled on initial install. Some of those services will remain disabled
    29: # forever, while others could be enabled by the various applications running
    30: # on the Delphix Appliance.
    31: #
    32: # Our approach is to mask services that need to be disabled. Masking a service
    33: # instead of just disabling it has 2 advantages:
    34: #  1. A service that is just disabled will not be started automatically by
    35: #     systemd on boot, however it can be started by another service if it has
    36: #     a certain set of dependencies on it (such as "Requires", "PartOf"). A
    37: #     service that is masked cannot be started in any case (although a
    38: #     service that is already running and has just been masked will not be
    39: #     stopped automatically).
    40: #  2. A service that is disabled can get re-enabled by dpkg maintenance scripts
    41: #     when the package that provides that service is upgraded. A service that
    42: #     is masked will not be unmasked.
    43: #
    44: # While masking a service is sufficient, we also disable most of the services
    45: # that we mask. This is not strictly necessary, but is done to remain
    46: # consistent with how we did things in the past. Our current logic that deals
    47: # with re-enabling those services will both unmask and enable # them.
    48: #
    49: # We have divided the disabling and masking of the services in multiple
    50: # code blocks to group together services that are handled in the same way by
    51: # the appliance.
    52: #
    53: # Note that if you want to modify this list make sure to also update
    54: # the logic in fix_and_migrate_services() that is invoked during upgrade.
    55: # You may also want to look at the logic that handles enabling disabling
    56: # services in dlpx-app-gate.

    58: 
    59: #
    60: # The services in this section should always remain disabled & masked.
    61: #
    62: - name: Disable and mask services that should never run
    63:   shell: |
    64:     systemctl disable {{ item }}
    65:     systemctl mask {{ item }}
    66:   with_items:
    67:     - fluentd.service
    68:     - nginx.service
    69:     - postgresql.service
    70:     - telegraf.service
    71:     - influxdb.service
    72: 
    73: #
    74: # The services in this section should be disabled & masked initially, but
    75: # can be later dynamically enabled by the appliance.
    76: #
    77: # delphix-fluentd.service and delphix-masking.service are owned by the
    78: # delphix-masking package, which isn't installed on variants (DCT, UCF)
    79: # that don't include the masking-common role; "disable" on a unit that
    80: # doesn't exist fails, so it's allowed to fail here. "mask" always
    81: # succeeds regardless of whether the unit exists.
    82: #
    83: - name: Disable and mask services that should not be running by default
    84:   shell: |
    85:     systemctl disable {{ item }} || true
    86:     systemctl mask {{ item }}
    87:   with_items:

    89:     - delphix-masking.service
    90:     - chrony.service
    91:     - snmpd.service

    95: # NFSv3 services so that they don't get automatically started at boot via
    96: # dependencies. The virtualization software is responsible for unmasking and
    97: # starting these services if NFSv3 needed at runtime.
    98: #
    99: - name: Mask NFSv3 services that should not be started automatically
   100:   command: "systemctl mask {{ item }}"

   102:     - rpcbind.service
   103:     - rpcbind.socket
   104:     - rpc-statd.service

   108: # gets started via a dependency of delphix-virtualization.

   110: - name: Disable docker
   111:   command: "systemctl disable {{ item }}"
   112:   with_items:
   113:     - docker.service

name: roles/authelia/tasks/admin_groups.yml
review_question: Is this Ansible artifact excessively large and in need of decomposition?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Reconcile the operator account's group membership on EVERY converge.
     3: #
     4: # users.yml is seeded create-if-absent (the argon2 hash is salted, so
     5: # re-rendering it would rotate the password on every run). That is correct for
     6: # the credential and wrong for group membership: a group added to the template
     7: # alone reaches a fresh deployment only, and on an existing one the converge
     8: # reports changed=0 while the group the operator needs is simply absent. Adding
     9: # `terrakube-admins` to the template was exactly that — a change that read as
    10: # applied and granted nothing.
    11: #
    12: # So membership is merged into the live file here instead. Additive by design:
    13: # groups present on the guest but not in authelia_admin_groups are left alone,
    14: # because the portal and any hand-grant are also writers of this file. Nothing
    15: # but the groups list is rewritten, and the task is a no-op once converged.
    16: 
    17: - name: Read the live users database
    18:   ansible.builtin.slurp:
    19:     src: "{{ authelia_users_file }}"
    20:   register: authelia_users_raw
    21:   no_log: true
    22: 
    23: - name: Resolve the operator's current and required groups
    24:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    25:     # `| default([], true)` on the groups read: a user block with `groups:` and
    26:     # nothing under it parses as null, not as an empty list, and union() on null
    27:     # raises rather than returning the required set.
    28:     authelia_admin_groups_current: >-
    29:       {{ ((authelia_users_raw.content | b64decode | from_yaml).users[authelia_admin_user].groups
    30:           | default([], true)) }}
    31:   no_log: true
    32: 
    33: - name: Fail when Terrakube SSO is enabled but its admin group did not resolve
    34:   ansible.builtin.assert:
    35:     that:
    36:       - authelia_terrakube_admin_group | length > 0
    37:     fail_msg: >-
    38:       authelia_terrakube_sso_enabled is true but DEX_GITHUB_ORG / DEX_GITHUB_TEAM
    39:       are not both set in the converge environment, so the org-qualified Terrakube
    40:       admin group could not be composed. Authelia would emit no Terrakube group at
    41:       all and the operator would authenticate to Terrakube with no rights. Set both
    42:       (they are the same two values the Terrakube compose file composes
    43:       TERRAKUBE_ADMIN_GROUP from) or leave authelia_terrakube_sso_enabled false.
    44:     success_msg: "Terrakube admin group resolved."
    45:   when: authelia_terrakube_sso_enabled | bool
    46: 
    47: - name: Grant the operator any required group it is missing
    48:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    49:     authelia_admin_groups_merged: >-
    50:       {{ authelia_admin_groups_current | union(authelia_admin_groups) }}
    51:   no_log: true
    52: 
    53: - name: Update the operator's group membership
    54:   when: authelia_admin_groups_merged | symmetric_difference(authelia_admin_groups_current) | length > 0
    55:   # lineinfile is deliberately not used: the groups list is multi-line, and a
    56:   # regex edit of a YAML sequence is how these files get corrupted. The whole
    57:   # document is re-emitted from the parsed structure with only the groups key
    58:   # replaced, so the password hash is carried through verbatim rather than
    59:   # re-generated.
    60:   ansible.builtin.copy:
    61:     content: >-
    62:       {{ (authelia_users_raw.content | b64decode | from_yaml)
    63:          | combine({'users': {authelia_admin_user: {'groups': authelia_admin_groups_merged}}},
    64:                    recursive=True)
    65:          | to_nice_yaml(indent=2) }}
    66:     dest: "{{ authelia_users_file }}"
    67:     owner: "{{ authelia_users_file_owner }}"
    68:     group: "{{ authelia_group }}"
    69:     mode: "0640"
    70:   no_log: true
    71:   notify: Restart authelia

source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Each Terrakube workspace policy references its workspace BY LIST INDEX
     3: # (openbao_terrakube_workspaces[N]) while carrying the workspace's name in its
     4: # own `name`. Nothing structural keeps the two in step: inserting a workspace
     5: # anywhere but the end, or mistyping an index, silently points a policy at a
     6: # DIFFERENT workspace — which grants that workspace's KV paths to the wrong
     7: # job identity and reads as a working converge.
     8: #
     9: # Compare the two ORDERED lists rather than their sets: a set comparison passes
    10: # on exactly the swap this is guarding against, since both names are still
    11: # present.
    12: - name: Assert every Terrakube workspace policy names the workspace it points at
    13:   ansible.builtin.assert:
    14:     that:
    15:       - _tk_policy_names == _tk_workspace_derived_names
    16:     fail_msg: >-
    17:       A Terrakube workspace policy references the wrong entry in
    18:       openbao_terrakube_workspaces. Declared policy names:
    19:       {{ _tk_policy_names }}; names derived from the workspaces each one
    20:       actually points at: {{ _tk_workspace_derived_names }}.
    21:     success_msg: "All {{ _tk_policy_names | length }} Terrakube workspace policies point at their own workspace."
    22:   vars:
    23:     _tk_policies: "{{ openbao_base_policies | selectattr('workspace', 'defined') | list }}"
    24:     _tk_policy_names: "{{ _tk_policies | map(attribute='name') | list }}"
    25:     _tk_workspace_derived_names: >-
    26:       {{ _tk_policies | map(attribute='workspace.name')
    27:          | map('regex_replace', '^', 'terrakube-') | list }}
    28:   run_once: true
    29:   delegate_to: localhost
    30:   become: false
    31: 
    32: # A reconcile-mode run may manage only what its OWN policy grants. That policy
    33: # is excluded from the set reconcile can rewrite (it cannot widen its own
    34: # grants), so the live policy drifts BEHIND the declared set the moment a new
    35: # policy is declared -- and every read/write of the new name then 403s.
    36: #
    37: # Ask the server what this token can actually do rather than inferring it from
    38: # the declared set, and fail LOUDLY naming the shortfall. Silently narrowing to
    39: # what happens to work is the exact false green this block exists to prevent:
    40: # a declared policy would never be written and nothing would say so.
    41: # The prefix is added by matching '^' rather than capturing the whole name and
    42: # substituting \1. A backreference does not survive the trip: YAML, Jinja and
    43: # `command`'s shlex.split each get a say in what a backslash means, and the net
    44: # effect was that all 60 paths rendered as the single literal
    45: # `sys/policies/acl/1` -- a policy that does not exist, so the server answered
    46: # `deny` and the gate concluded the identity could write nothing. It had never
    47: # once asked about a real path.
    48: - name: Ask the server which declared policies this identity may actually write
    49:   ansible.builtin.command:
    50:     cmd: >-
    51:       bao write -format=json sys/capabilities-self
    52:       {{ openbao_manageable_policies
    53:          | map(attribute='name')
    54:          | map('regex_replace', '^', 'paths=sys/policies/acl/')
    55:          | join(' ') }}
    56:   environment:
    57:     BAO_ADDR: "{{ openbao_api_addr }}"
    58:     BAO_TOKEN: "{{ openbao_bootstrap_token }}"
    59:   register: openbao_policy_capabilities
    60:   changed_when: false
    61:   failed_when: false
    62:   no_log: true
    63:   when:
    64:     - openbao_bootstrap_token is defined
    65:     - openbao_reconcile_mode | default(false)
    66: 
    67: # sys/capabilities-self returns the per-path capability lists BOTH at the top
    68: # level and under `data`, and which of the two a given client surfaces is not
    69: # something to bet a hard failure on. Reading only `data` yielded an empty dict
    70: # against a live policy that demonstrably grants create/read/update on every
    71: # path asked about -- and an empty dict reads as "denied everything", so the
    72: # gate blocked a converge that should have proceeded.
    73: - name: Resolve what the server said this identity may write
    74:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    75:     openbao_policy_caps: >-
    76:       {{ (_body.get('data', {}) | combine(_body)) | dict2items
    77:          | selectattr('key', 'match', '^sys/policies/acl/') | items2dict }}
    78:   vars:
    79:     _body: "{{ openbao_policy_capabilities.stdout | default('{}') | from_json }}"
    80:   # Keep only real policy paths, rather than removing a hand-listed set of
    81:   # envelope keys. The response also carries `capabilities`, `mount_type`,
    82:   # `mount_class` and friends, and any future field would join them -- a
    83:   # denylist would have to grow to stay correct. A stray key surviving here
    84:   # would be compared against declared policy NAMES below (the prefix is
    85:   # stripped, not filtered, at that point), so a collision would mark a policy
    86:   # writable that is not: a false green in the guard built to prevent one.
    87:   when:
    88:     - openbao_bootstrap_token is defined
    89:     - openbao_reconcile_mode | default(false)
    90:     - (openbao_policy_capabilities.rc | default(1)) == 0
    91: 
    92: # An uninformative probe is NOT a denial. If the response carried capability
    93: # entries for FEWER paths than were asked about, the probe itself is broken (a
    94: # shape change, a malformed request) and reading the gap as a permission finding
    95: # would be a confident false red -- the same absent-vs-denied confusion this
    96: # whole block exists to eliminate. Fail, but say which failure it is.
    97: #
    98: # The count, not merely zero: the backreference bug asked about one literal path
    99: # and got ONE well-formed entry back, so a `== 0` arm did not fire and the gate
   100: # went on to report a unanimous false denial. A short answer is the direct
   101: # signature of a probe that asked the wrong question, and neither a zero-check
   102: # nor a type-check sees it -- the values were valid capability lists, just for a
   103: # path nobody declared.
   104: - name: FAIL -- the capability probe did not answer about every path it asked about
   105:   ansible.builtin.fail:
   106:     msg: >-
   107:       Asked sys/capabilities-self about
   108:       {{ openbao_manageable_policies | length }} policy paths and the response
   109:       carried a capability entry for only
   110:       {{ openbao_policy_caps | default({}) | length }} of them. That is a broken
   111:       probe, not a permission finding -- do not read a short answer as "this
   112:       identity may write nothing". Check the request shape and the response
   113:       envelope before concluding anything about grants.
   114:   when:
   115:     - openbao_bootstrap_token is defined
   116:     - openbao_reconcile_mode | default(false)
   117:     - (openbao_policy_capabilities.rc | default(1)) == 0
   118:     - openbao_manageable_policies | length > 0
   119:     - >-
   120:       (openbao_policy_caps | default({}) | length)
   121:       < (openbao_manageable_policies | length)
   122: 
   123: - name: FAIL -- the reconcile identity cannot manage every declared policy
   124:   vars:
   125:     _caps: "{{ openbao_policy_caps | default({}) }}"
   126:     _unwritable: >-
   127:       {{ openbao_manageable_policies | map(attribute='name') | reject('in',
   128:          (_caps | dict2items
   129:                 | selectattr('value', 'contains', 'update')
   130:                 | map(attribute='key')
   131:                 | map('regex_replace', '^sys/policies/acl/', '')
   132:                 | list)) | list | sort }}
   133:   ansible.builtin.fail:
   134:     msg: >-
   135:       The openbao-reconcile identity is declared as managing
   136:       {{ openbao_manageable_policies | length }} policies but the live
   137:       openbao-reconcile policy grants update on none of these
   138:       {{ _unwritable | length }}: {{ _unwritable | join(', ') }}.
   139:       Reconcile CANNOT widen its own grants -- openbao-reconcile is in
   140:       openbao_reconcile_excluded_policies by design -- so this only clears with
   141:       one operator-token run (OPENBAO_PROVISIONING_TOKEN), which rewrites the
   142:       reconcile policy from the current declared set. Refusing to continue:
   143:       writing only the reachable subset would leave the rest declared but never
   144:       written, with the converge still reporting success.
   145:   when:
   146:     - openbao_bootstrap_token is defined
   147:     - openbao_reconcile_mode | default(false)
   148:     - (openbao_policy_capabilities.rc | default(1)) == 0
   149:     - _unwritable | length > 0
   150: 
   151: # Rendered on the CONTROLLER, not the target. The previous shape wrote each
   152: # policy to the guest with `template`, read it back with `slurp`, and deleted it
   153: # again -- three remote round trips per policy purely to move content this
   154: # process already had in memory. Over 60 policies that is 180 operations on a
   155: # proxmox_pct_remote connection, and each one is a full paramiko connect plus a
   156: # `pct exec`: the render step alone measured 776 SECONDS (12.9 min, ~13s per
   157: # policy) writing a few KB per file.
   158: #
   159: # `lookup('template', ...)` resolves against the same role templates/ directory
   160: # the module used and renders with the same variable context, so the content is
   161: # identical -- it just never leaves the controller. The write below feeds it to
   162: # `bao policy write` on stdin, so no file is created and none has to be cleaned
   163: # up. Remote operations for this phase: 180 -> 0.
   164: - name: Render the RBAC policies on the controller
   165:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   166:     openbao_rendered_policy_map: >-
   167:       {{ openbao_rendered_policy_map | default({})
   168:          | combine({ item.name: lookup('template', item.template) | trim }) }}
   169:   loop: "{{ openbao_manageable_policies }}"
   170:   loop_control:
   171:     label: "{{ item.name }}"
   172:   no_log: true
   173:   when: openbao_bootstrap_token is defined
   174: 
   175: - name: List existing policies
   176:   ansible.builtin.command:
   177:     cmd: bao policy list -format=json
   178:   environment:
   179:     BAO_ADDR: "{{ openbao_api_addr }}"
   180:     BAO_TOKEN: "{{ openbao_bootstrap_token }}"
   181:   register: openbao_policies_raw
   182:   no_log: true
   183:   changed_when: false
   184:   when: openbao_bootstrap_token is defined
   185: 
   186: - name: Read existing RBAC policy contents
   187:   ansible.builtin.command:
   188:     cmd: "bao policy read -format=json {{ item.name }}"
   189:   environment:
   190:     BAO_ADDR: "{{ openbao_api_addr }}"
   191:     BAO_TOKEN: "{{ openbao_bootstrap_token }}"
   192:   loop: "{{ openbao_manageable_policies }}"
   193:   loop_control:
   194:     label: "{{ item.name }}"
   195:   register: openbao_existing_policy_reads
   196:   no_log: true
   197:   changed_when: false
   198:   # Every other probe in this file tolerates a non-zero rc; this one did not, so
   199:   # a single denied read aborted the whole block before any policy was written.
   200:   # The map build below already guards on `rc == 0`, so a failed read is an
   201:   # expected, handled input -- not a reason to stop. The capability gate above
   202:   # is what turns a genuine scope shortfall into a loud failure.
   203:   failed_when: false
   204:   when:
   205:     - openbao_bootstrap_token is defined
   206:     - item.name in (openbao_policies_raw.stdout | from_json)
   207: 
   208: # Both sides are `trim`ed and read from the CORRECT key, because the write below
   209: # is a no-op only when the two compare equal -- and it was never equal:
   210: #
   211: #   * `bao policy read -format=json` returns {"policy": ...} at TOP LEVEL. The
   212: #     old expression read `.data.policy`, which does not exist, so every entry
   213: #     resolved to '' and every policy looked changed on every converge.
   214: #   * The server appends a trailing newline on write, so even with the right key
   215: #     the stored text is the rendered text plus "\n" and an exact != is always
   216: #     true.
   217: #
   218: # Measured live: rendered 475 bytes vs stored 476, differing only in that
   219: # newline, `stripped_equal` true on every sampled policy. Either defect alone
   220: # rewrites all 56 policies on every run while honestly reporting "changed", so
   221: # fixing only one would have looked like a fix and changed nothing.
   222: - name: Build the existing RBAC policy content map
   223:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   224:     openbao_existing_policy_map: >-
   225:       {{ openbao_existing_policy_map | default({})
   226:          | combine({ item.item.name: ((item.stdout | default('{}') | from_json).policy | default('')) | trim }) }}
   227:   loop: "{{ openbao_existing_policy_reads.results | default([]) }}"
   228:   loop_control:
   229:     label: "{{ item.item.name }}"
   230:   no_log: true
   231:   when:
   232:     - openbao_bootstrap_token is defined
   233:     - not (item.skipped | default(false))
   234:     - (item.rc | default(1)) == 0
   235: 
   236: - name: Write the RBAC policies that are missing or changed
   237:   ansible.builtin.command:
   238:     cmd: "bao policy write {{ item.name }} -"
   239:     stdin: "{{ (openbao_rendered_policy_map | default({}))[item.name] }}"
   240:   environment:
   241:     BAO_ADDR: "{{ openbao_api_addr }}"
   242:     BAO_TOKEN: "{{ openbao_bootstrap_token }}"
   243:   loop: "{{ openbao_manageable_policies }}"
   244:   loop_control:
   245:     label: "{{ item.name }}"
   246:   no_log: true
   247:   changed_when: true
   248:   when:
   249:     - openbao_bootstrap_token is defined
   250:     - >-
   251:       item.name not in (openbao_policies_raw.stdout | from_json)
   252:       or
   253:       (openbao_existing_policy_map | default({})).get(item.name, '')
   254:       !=
   255:       (openbao_rendered_policy_map | default({})).get(item.name, '')

source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Kubernetes does not permit changing a StatefulSet volumeClaimTemplate in
     3: # place. Grow the live PVCs first, orphan only the controller, and let the
     4: # owning chart/operator recreate it around the same pods and claims.
     5: 
     6: - name: 'Read {{ storage_reconcile_statefulset }} StatefulSet storage contract'
     7:   kubernetes.core.k8s_info:
     8:     api_version: apps/v1
     9:     kind: StatefulSet
    10:     namespace: '{{ storage_reconcile_namespace }}'
    11:     name: '{{ storage_reconcile_statefulset }}'
    12:   register: _storage_reconcile_sts
    13: 
    14: - name: 'Resolve {{ storage_reconcile_statefulset }} claim-template size'
    15:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    16:     _storage_reconcile_current: >-
    17:       {{
    18:         (
    19:           _storage_reconcile_sts.resources[0].spec.volumeClaimTemplates
    20:           | selectattr('metadata.name', 'equalto', storage_reconcile_claim)
    21:           | map(attribute='spec.resources.requests.storage')
    22:           | first
    23:         )
    24:         if _storage_reconcile_sts.resources | length > 0 else ''
    25:       }}
    26: 
    27: - name: 'Reject {{ storage_reconcile_statefulset }} storage shrink attempts'
    28:   ansible.builtin.assert:
    29:     that:
    30:       - _storage_reconcile_current is match('^[1-9][0-9]*Gi$')
    31:       - storage_reconcile_desired is match('^[1-9][0-9]*Gi$')
    32:       - (storage_reconcile_desired | regex_replace('Gi$', '') | int) >= (_storage_reconcile_current | regex_replace('Gi$', '') | int)
    33:     fail_msg: >-
    34:       Refusing to shrink {{ storage_reconcile_namespace }}/{{ storage_reconcile_statefulset }}
    35:       storage from {{ _storage_reconcile_current }} to {{ storage_reconcile_desired }}.
    36:   when: _storage_reconcile_current | length > 0
    37: 
    38: - name: 'Read {{ storage_reconcile_statefulset }} live claims'
    39:   kubernetes.core.k8s_info:
    40:     api_version: v1
    41:     kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
    42:     namespace: '{{ storage_reconcile_namespace }}'
    43:     name: '{{ storage_reconcile_claim }}-{{ storage_reconcile_statefulset }}-{{ item }}'
    44:   loop: >-
    45:     {{ range(0, _storage_reconcile_sts.resources[0].spec.replicas | int) | list
    46:        if (_storage_reconcile_sts.resources | default([])) | length > 0 else [] }}
    47:   register: _storage_reconcile_claims
    48: 
    49: - name: 'Reject {{ storage_reconcile_statefulset }} live-claim shrink attempts'
    50:   ansible.builtin.assert:
    51:     that:
    52:       - (storage_reconcile_desired | regex_replace('Gi$', '') | int) >= (item.resources[0].spec.resources.requests.storage | regex_replace('Gi$', '') | int)
    53:     quiet: true
    54:     fail_msg: >-
    55:       Refusing to shrink {{ storage_reconcile_namespace }}/{{ item.resources[0].metadata.name }}
    56:       from {{ item.resources[0].spec.resources.requests.storage }} to {{ storage_reconcile_desired }}.
    57:   loop: '{{ _storage_reconcile_claims.results | default([]) }}'
    58:   loop_control:
    59:     label: '{{ item.item | default("unknown") }}'
    60:   when: (item.resources | default([])) | length == 1
    61:   no_log: true
    62: 
    63: - name: 'Expand {{ storage_reconcile_statefulset }} claims before template reconciliation'
    64:   # JSON Patch changes only the permitted storage request. A merge patch can
    65:   # serialize defaulted empty fields (notably volumeName) and Kubernetes then
    66:   # rejects an otherwise valid growth while a newly scaled claim is Pending.
    67:   kubernetes.core.k8s_json_patch:
    68:     api_version: v1
    69:     kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
    70:     name: '{{ item.resources[0].metadata.name }}'
    71:     namespace: '{{ storage_reconcile_namespace }}'
    72:     patch:
    73:       - op: replace
    74:         path: /spec/resources/requests/storage
    75:         value: '{{ storage_reconcile_desired }}'
    76:   loop: '{{ _storage_reconcile_claims.results | default([]) }}'
    77:   loop_control:
    78:     label: '{{ item.item | default("unknown") }}'
    79:   when:
    80:     - _storage_reconcile_current | length > 0
    81:     - (item.resources | default([])) | length == 1
    82:     # Kubernetes permits storage growth only after a claim is Bound. A Pending
    83:     # claim created during an operator scale-up is reconciled after adoption.
    84:     - item.resources[0].status.phase | default('') == 'Bound'
    85:     - (storage_reconcile_desired | regex_replace('Gi$', '') | int) > (item.resources[0].spec.resources.requests.storage | regex_replace('Gi$', '') | int)
    86: 
    87: - name: 'Orphan {{ storage_reconcile_statefulset }} pods and claims for immutable template growth'
    88:   kubernetes.core.k8s:
    89:     state: absent
    90:     api_version: apps/v1
    91:     kind: StatefulSet
    92:     namespace: '{{ storage_reconcile_namespace }}'
    93:     name: '{{ storage_reconcile_statefulset }}'
    94:     delete_options:
    95:       propagationPolicy: Orphan
    96:     wait: '{{ storage_reconcile_wait | default(true) | bool }}'
    97:   when:
    98:     - _storage_reconcile_current | length > 0
    99:     - _storage_reconcile_current != storage_reconcile_desired
   100:     - storage_reconcile_orphan | default(true) | bool

source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Capture the tail of the Glance API log from every testbed host into the job
     3: # output, so a failing Octavia/Glance image import can be diagnosed.
     4: #
     5: # Glance writes its log to a file -- kolla-ansible sets
     6: # "log_file = /var/log/kolla/glance/glance-api.log" -- and not to the
     7: # container's stdout, so "docker logs glance_api" does not contain the
     8: # web-download import error. The image-import step ("osism manage image
     9: # octavia") only reports that the image is "stuck in queued"; the actual reason
    10: # (download / qcow2->raw conversion / Ceph write) lives only in the on-host
    11: # glance-api.log. Capturing it here lets zuul-analyzer (which only consumes the
    12: # job output) classify the failing stage. See the issue-tracker entry
    13: # "octavia-stuck-queued".
    14: #
    15: # This runs in post-run, before the cleanup play tears the environment down.
    16: # The orchestrator can only reach the manager directly (the nodes sit on a
    17: # private network), so we hop through the manager, which fans out to every
    18: # deployed host. The play is best-effort and must never fail the job.
    19: - name: Collect Glance API logs play
    20:   hosts: all
    21: 
    22:   vars_files:
    23:     - vars/mappings.yml
    24:     - vars/repositories.yml
    25: 
    26:   vars:
    27:     basepath: "{{ ansible_user_dir }}/src/{{ repositories['testbed']['path'] }}"
    28:     terraform_path: "{{ basepath }}/terraform"
    29:     glance_log_tail_lines: 2000
    30: 
    31:   tasks:
    32:     - name: Set cloud fact (Zuul deployment)
    33:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    34:         cloud: "{{ cloud_envs[hostvars[groups['all'][0]]['nodepool']['label']] }}"
    35:       when: "'nodepool' in hostvars[groups['all'][0]]"
    36: 
    37:     - name: Set cloud fact (local deployment)
    38:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    39:         cloud: "{{ testbed_cloud | default('ci') }}"
    40:       when: "'nodepool' not in hostvars[groups['all'][0]]"
    41: 
    42:     - name: Read the manager address
    43:       ansible.builtin.slurp:
    44:         src: "{{ terraform_path }}/.MANAGER_ADDRESS.{{ cloud }}"
    45:       register: _glance_manager_address
    46:       failed_when: false
    47: 
    48:     - name: Capture the Glance API log from all testbed hosts
    49:       when: _glance_manager_address.content is defined
    50:       vars:
    51:         manager_host: "{{ _glance_manager_address.content | b64decode | trim | split('=') | last | replace('\"', '') }}"
    52:       ansible.builtin.shell:
    53:         cmd: |
    54:           set -o pipefail
    55:           ssh \
    56:             -i {{ terraform_path }}/.id_rsa.{{ cloud }} \
    57:             -o BatchMode=yes \
    58:             -o ConnectTimeout=10 \
    59:             -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no \
    60:             -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \
    61:             -o LogLevel=ERROR \
    62:             dragon@{{ manager_host }} 'bash -s' <<'REMOTE'
    63:           set -uo pipefail
    64:           hosts=$(osism get hosts 2>/dev/null | awk -F'|' '/^\|/ {gsub(/^ +| +$/,"",$2); if ($2!="" && $2!="Host" && $2!~/^-+$/) print $2}')
    65:           for h in $hosts; do
    66:             echo "===== glance-api.log (tail -n {{ glance_log_tail_lines }}) @ ${h} ====="
    67:             ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o LogLevel=ERROR "${h}" '(sudo -n tail -n {{ glance_log_tail_lines }} /var/log/kolla/glance/glance-api.log || tail -n {{ glance_log_tail_lines }} /var/log/kolla/glance/glance-api.log) 2>/dev/null || echo "(no readable glance-api.log on this host)"'
    68:             echo
    69:           done
    70:           REMOTE
    71:       args:
    72:         executable: /bin/bash
    73:       register: _glance_logs
    74:       changed_when: false
    75:       failed_when: false
    76: 
    77:     # Surface stdout *and* stderr: when the SSH to the manager fails before
    78:     # producing output, the reason lives in stderr and stdout_lines is an empty
    79:     # (defined) list, so a plain `default` would not fire. `default(..., true)`
    80:     # also substitutes the falsy/empty result.
    81:     - name: Show the captured Glance API log

    85:               + (_glance_logs.stderr_lines | default([])))
    86:              | default(['(glance-api.log capture was skipped or produced no output)'], true) }}

1: ---
     2: # Gateway collector — OpenTelemetry-recommended "gateway pattern" implementation.
     3: # Called from setup.yml when `opentelemetry_gateway_enabled: true`, *before*
     4: # the helm task so the gateway collector spec AND its supporting resources
     5: # (htpasswd Secret + Ingress) are included in the chart values.
     6: #
     7: # All resources go through helm via:
     8: #   - `collectors.<gateway_name>` (the OpenTelemetryCollector CR + the
     9: #     operator-spawned Service/Deployment) → driven by
    10: #     `opentelemetry_collectors[<gateway_name>]`
    11: #   - `extraObjects[]` (Secret + Ingress) → driven by
    12: #     `opentelemetry_additional_config.extraObjects`
    13: #
    14: # That way helm owns the full lifecycle: a `helm upgrade` after disabling
    15: # the gateway tears everything down, and credential rotation is reflected
    16: # through a pod-annotation checksum so the operator triggers a rollout.
    17: 
    18: - name: "Compute gateway derived values"
    19:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    20:     _opentelemetry_gateway_full_name: "{{ opentelemetry_release_name }}-{{ opentelemetry_gateway_name }}"
    21:     _opentelemetry_gateway_htpasswd_secret_name: "{{ opentelemetry_release_name }}-{{ opentelemetry_gateway_name }}-htpasswd"
    22:     _opentelemetry_gateway_auth_enabled: "{{ (opentelemetry_gateway_htpasswd | default('') | length) > 0 }}"
    23: 
    24: - name: "Build the gateway collector spec"
    25:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    26:     opentelemetry_collectors: >-
    27:       {{
    28:         (opentelemetry_collectors | default({}))
    29:         | combine({ opentelemetry_gateway_name: _opentelemetry_gateway_collector_spec }, recursive=True)
    30:       }}
    31:   vars:
    32:     _volumes: >-
    33:       {{
    34:         [{
    35:           'name': 'htpasswd',
    36:           'secret': {'secretName': _opentelemetry_gateway_htpasswd_secret_name}
    37:         }]
    38:         if _opentelemetry_gateway_auth_enabled else []
    39:       }}
    40:     _volume_mounts: >-
    41:       {{
    42:         [{
    43:           'name': 'htpasswd',
    44:           'mountPath': '/etc/otel-auth',
    45:           'readOnly': true
    46:         }]
    47:         if _opentelemetry_gateway_auth_enabled else []
    48:       }}
    49:     # Credential rotation: the basicauth/server extension caches the
    50:     # htpasswd file at startup, so secret content changes only take effect
    51:     # when the pod restarts. Putting a checksum of the content in
    52:     # podAnnotations makes the operator roll the pod whenever the content
    53:     # differs from the previous apply.
    54:     _pod_annotations: >-
    55:       {{
    56:         {'checksum/htpasswd': (opentelemetry_gateway_htpasswd | hash('sha256'))}
    57:         if _opentelemetry_gateway_auth_enabled else {}
    58:       }}
    59:     _extensions: >-
    60:       {{
    61:         {'basicauth/server': {'htpasswd': {'file': '/etc/otel-auth/htpasswd'}}}
    62:         if _opentelemetry_gateway_auth_enabled else {}
    63:       }}
    64:     _service_extensions: >-
    65:       {{
    66:         ['basicauth/server']
    67:         if _opentelemetry_gateway_auth_enabled else []
    68:       }}
    69:     # Auto-wire basicauth/server onto the OTLP HTTP receiver. We deep-merge
    70:     # so the user keeps full control of receiver options (compression,
    71:     # max_recv_msg_size, …).
    72:     _otlp_http_auth_overlay:
    73:       otlp:
    74:         protocols:
    75:           http:
    76:             auth:
    77:               authenticator: "basicauth/server"
    78:     _receivers: >-
    79:       {{
    80:         opentelemetry_gateway_receivers
    81:         | combine(_otlp_http_auth_overlay, recursive=True)
    82:         if _opentelemetry_gateway_auth_enabled
    83:         else opentelemetry_gateway_receivers
    84:       }}
    85:     # If the user did not provide explicit pipelines, route every receiver +
    86:     # processor + exporter into metrics & logs pipelines. Works for the
    87:     # common case of homogeneous OTLP exporters; override when you have
    88:     # signal-specific routing.
    89:     _default_pipelines:
    90:       metrics:
    91:         receivers: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_receivers.keys() | list }}"
    92:         processors: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_processors.keys() | list }}"
    93:         exporters: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_exporters.keys() | list }}"
    94:       logs:
    95:         receivers: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_receivers.keys() | list }}"
    96:         processors: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_processors.keys() | list }}"
    97:         exporters: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_exporters.keys() | list }}"
    98:     _pipelines: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_pipelines if (opentelemetry_gateway_pipelines | length > 0) else _default_pipelines }}"
    99:     _opentelemetry_gateway_collector_spec:
   100:       enabled: true
   101:       mode: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_mode }}"
   102:       replicas: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_replicas }}"
   103:       # Predictable service name (`<release>-<gateway_name>-collector`),
   104:       # otherwise the chart defaults to `<release>-collector` which
   105:       # collides with any other non-daemon collector. Required for the
   106:       # Ingress backend reference below.
   107:       fullnameOverride: "{{ _opentelemetry_gateway_full_name }}"
   108:       resources: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_resources }}"
   109:       volumes: "{{ _volumes }}"
   110:       volumeMounts: "{{ _volume_mounts }}"
   111:       podAnnotations: "{{ _pod_annotations }}"
   112:       config:
   113:         extensions: "{{ _extensions }}"
   114:         receivers: "{{ _receivers }}"
   115:         processors: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_processors }}"
   116:         exporters: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_exporters }}"
   117:         service:
   118:           extensions: "{{ _service_extensions }}"
   119:           pipelines: "{{ _pipelines }}"
   120: 
   121: - name: "Inject the gateway Secret + Ingress as chart extraObjects"
   122:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   123:     opentelemetry_additional_config: >-
   124:       {{
   125:         (opentelemetry_additional_config | default({}))
   126:         | combine({
   127:             'extraObjects': (
   128:               ((opentelemetry_additional_config | default({})).extraObjects | default([]))
   129:               + _gateway_extra_objects
   130:             )
   131:           })
   132:       }}
   133:   when: _gateway_extra_objects | length > 0
   134:   vars:
   135:     _htpasswd_secret_obj:
   136:       apiVersion: "v1"
   137:       kind: "Secret"

   142:       stringData:
   143:         htpasswd: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_htpasswd }}"
   144:     _ingress_obj:
   145:       apiVersion: "networking.k8s.io/v1"

   148:         name: "{{ _opentelemetry_gateway_full_name }}"

     2: # Re-pair playbook for zeroclaw restart (issue #437).
     3: #
     4: # The systemd restart itself happens in start.yaml / stop.yaml (driven by
     5: # lifecycle.restart_agent's stop -> start path). This playbook runs *after*
     6: # the daemon is back up: it waits for /health/providers to respond, then
     7: # performs the pair handshake. The new bearer token is emitted as a
     8: # cacheable host fact so lifecycle.restart_agent can persist it to
     9: # hosts.json under agents.<n>.config.gateway.auth.
    10: #
    11: # Without this step, a `clawctl agent restart zeroclaw-…` would silently
    12: # invalidate hosts.json's bearer (the daemon mints a fresh token on
    13: # startup, so the old token in hosts.json no longer matches whatever the
    14: # daemon will enforce).
    15: 
    16: # ATX W-SEC-4: no `become: yes` — every task in this play (the
    17: # /health/providers probe + the included pair.yaml handshake) hits
    18: # loopback HTTP only. Privilege escalation here would broaden blast
    19: # radius for zero benefit; if a future task needs root, add `become`
    20: # at the task level (not the play level).
    21: - hosts: all
    22:   vars:
    23:     gateway_port: "{{ config.gateway.port }}"
    24:     gateway_local_base: "http://127.0.0.1:{{ gateway_port }}"
    25:   tasks:
    26:     - name: Probe /health/providers
    27:       ansible.builtin.uri:
    28:         url: "{{ gateway_local_base }}/health/providers"
    29:         method: GET
    30:         status_code: [200, 401]
    31:         timeout: 5
    32:       register: health_probe
    33:       retries: 30
    34:       delay: 2
    35:       until: health_probe.status in [200, 401]
    36:       no_log: true
    37: 
    38:     - name: Run zeroclaw pair handshake

    48:         - not (memory_filename is match('^memory/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$'))

    52:         path: "/home/{{ agent_name }}/.zeroclaw/workspace"
